title: Part A: Trace Storage (Steps 1-7)
Phase B: Row selection checkbox slide-in
No CLI flag to evaluate against user's own documentation
description: The agent-evals CLI hardcodes doc_tree loading via load_doc_tree_for_source() which only supports the built-in 56-file sample fixture or pre-prepared dataset adapters. There is no --docs or --local flag to point at real user documentation. The end-to-end workflow (scan docs with agent-index → evaluate with agent-evals) requires users to either: (1) manually create a dataset adapter, or (2) hack the source.py routing. Need: a --docs <path> flag that calls agent_index.scanner.scan_local(), applies tier assignment, and passes the resulting DocTree to the evaluation runner. This is the critical missing link between the two packages.

title: Report aggregator CI uses z=1.96 instead of t-distribution for small sample sizes
Add configuration/setup and migration task types
description: The 11 task types miss two of the most common real-world agent documentation tasks: (1) CONFIGURATION TASKS: 'How do I configure X with settings Y and Z?' — tests whether the agent can synthesize a complete config file from scattered doc fragments, scored by config validity + completeness. (2) MIGRATION/UPGRADE TASKS: 'Upgrade from v2 to v3' — tests whether the agent can identify breaking changes, deprecated features, and produce a migration plan, scored by change coverage + correctness. (3) API INTEGRATION TASKS: 'Write code that calls the Widget API with auth' — tests end-to-end integration synthesis from API docs. These are the tasks where documentation format matters MOST because they require synthesizing information from multiple doc sections. The existing code_generation type is too generic to capture config/migration-specific patterns.

title: Add document freshness/staleness simulation
description: Real documentation is partially stale — some pages are current, some are months or years old, some are contradictory across versions. The temporal axis (10) only adds timestamps/version markers to docs but doesn't simulate the INFORMATION DECAY problem. Need: (1) inject deliberate version conflicts (v2 docs still present alongside v3), (2) test whether formats that emphasize recency help agents prefer newer info, (3) measure 'staleness tolerance' per format — how much outdated content can exist before accuracy drops, (4) simulate 'docs drift' where 20% of content is subtly wrong (not just deprecated). This matters because every real documentation corpus has staleness issues and the right format should help agents navigate them.

title: No 'apply optimal' workflow from Taguchi results to agent-index config
description: After running a Taguchi pipeline and identifying optimal factor levels (e.g., structure-3tier, metadata-with-summary, format-yaml), there is no automated way to translate those findings into an agent-index IndexConfig that implements those choices. The pipeline returns final_optimal as a dict of factor→level mappings, but users must manually: (1) interpret variant names back to config parameters, (2) write an agent-index.yaml by hand, (3) re-run agent-index with those settings. Need: an 'apply' command or export function that maps Taguchi optimal levels to IndexConfig fields (tier count, metadata inclusion, output format, etc.) and generates a ready-to-use agent-index.yaml.

title: Add actionable recommendations engine from Taguchi results
description: The pipeline produces S/N ratios, ANOVA tables, and optimal configurations, but no human-readable actionable guidance. A technical writer looking at 'axis_3: yaml, axis_1: 3tier, axis_8: section' doesn't know what to DO. Need: (1) natural language recommendation generator: 'Use 3-tier hierarchical structure with YAML format and section-level granularity. This combination outperforms alternatives by 23% on retrieval and code generation tasks.', (2) per-audience recommendations (DevRel team, solo dev, enterprise), (3) format-specific style guide generation from winning configurations, (4) confidence-rated recommendations (high/medium/low based on effect sizes and sample size), (5) 'avoid these' anti-patterns from worst-performing configurations. Without this, the framework is a research tool — with this, it becomes a documentation optimization product.

title: Progress callback shows no running cost during CLI evaluation
description: The progress callbacks in progress.py (_plain_callback and _rich_callback) only display task_id, variant_name, and score. They do not show accumulated cost, projected total cost, or budget utilization. During a long evaluation run, users have no CLI visibility into spend unless they also run the observatory dashboard. The TrialResult passed to the callback has cost data available. Need: add running cost total and budget percentage to the progress display. E.g., '[####----] 25% (50/200) task_001 | scale_50 | 0.85 | $0.42/$2.00 (21%)'.

title: Add code block formatting axis
description: No axis tests how CODE BLOCKS within documentation affect agent performance. Real docs are full of code examples. Need new axis testing: (1) code block density (no examples, inline only, full examples per section), (2) code block language tagging (```python vs untagged), (3) runnable vs pseudo-code examples, (4) code-before-explanation vs explanation-before-code ordering, (5) import statement inclusion/exclusion, (6) error handling in examples (complete vs minimal). This interacts heavily with code_generation and agentic task types. Currently the fixture docs have some code but it's not systematically varied as a treatment.

title: Add heading depth and semantic structure axis
description: The structure axis (1) tests flat/2tier/3tier/4tier but doesn't test HEADING SEMANTICS — how heading text itself affects navigation. Need new axis: (1) heading verbosity (terse 'Config' vs descriptive 'Database Configuration Options'), (2) heading hierarchy depth (2 levels vs 6 levels for same content), (3) numbered vs unnumbered headings, (4) question-style headings ('How do I configure X?') vs noun-style ('Configuration'), (5) heading-as-TOC (headings that preview their content) vs heading-as-label. LLMs use headings as primary navigation cues — this is likely a high-impact untested dimension.

title: Full-config.yaml example missing Taguchi/pipeline/observatory options
description: The examples/full-config.yaml only documents basic evaluation options (LLM settings, scope, execution, cost control, output). It is missing documentation for 15+ config keys that the CLI supports: mode (taguchi), models (multi-model list), pipeline (auto/semi), quality_type (larger_is_better/smaller_is_better/nominal_is_best), top_k, alpha, oa_type, report (html/md/both), store_traces, dashboard, dashboard_port, source (dataset selection), budget, model_budgets, resume, resume_pipeline. Users have no YAML reference for the advanced DOE/pipeline features and must read source code or CLI --help to discover them.

title: Phase B: Row hover elevation
Add multi-corpus generalization validation framework
description: The framework can't answer the fundamental question: 'Do these format recommendations work for MY docs, or only for YOUR test corpus?' Need: (1) corpus fingerprinting — characterize a doc corpus by size, complexity, code density, domain, language, (2) results portability analysis — measure how well Taguchi rankings from corpus A predict performance on corpus B, (3) conditional recommendations — 'for API-heavy docs, prefer X; for tutorial-heavy docs, prefer Y', (4) user-supplied corpus adapter — let someone plug in their own docs and get personalized recommendations. This requires both the real dataset work (#46) AND a meta-analysis layer that compares results ACROSS corpora. Without this, every result has an asterisk: 'valid only for our synthetic fixture.'

title: Pipeline resume reconstructs PhaseResult with empty trials, losing cost/token totals
description: When resuming a pipeline (pipeline.py lines 311-323, 344-350, 374-380), completed phases are reconstructed with trials=[] and no cost/token data. This means: (1) PipelineResult.total_trials undercounts (only new phase trials counted), (2) PipelineResult.total_cost undercounts (prior phase costs are 0.0 by default), (3) elapsed_seconds undercounts. The store has all trial data via get_trials(run_id) but it's not loaded during reconstruction. Need: either load trial aggregates from the observatory store (the get_run_summary method has total_cost/trial_count), or persist phase-level cost/token summaries alongside phase_results.

title: Add response calibration and confidence measurement
description: The framework measures ACCURACY but not CALIBRATION — whether the agent knows when it's uncertain. A format that produces 80% accuracy with 95% 'I'm confident' is worse than 80% accuracy with calibrated confidence. Need: (1) extract confidence signals from responses (hedging language, explicit confidence levels), (2) compute Expected Calibration Error (ECE) per variant, (3) measure selective accuracy — if the agent could abstain on uncertain answers, what's its accuracy on remaining ones?, (4) per-variant calibration curves, (5) combine with negative task type to measure whether format helps agent know its limits. This matters enormously for production agents — miscalibrated confidence leads to hallucination that users trust.

title: No CLI command for cross-run comparison
description: The observatory web API has a comparison endpoint (GET /api/compare?ids=run1,run2) but there is no CLI subcommand to compare two runs. Users who want to compare runs without launching the dashboard have no option. Need: an 'agent-evals compare <run_id_1> <run_id_2>' CLI command that shows side-by-side variant scores, cost deltas, and statistical significance of score differences between runs. Output as table to terminal or as a report file.

title: algorithmic_compress strips injection markers containing hyphens in marker_id
description: In transform.py:46-48, the regex that preserves injection markers during HTML comment removal uses \w+ which only matches [a-zA-Z0-9_]. Hyphens are not matched. If a user calls inject_into_file(path, content, marker_id='MY-DOCS'), the markers <\!-- MY-DOCS:START --> and <\!-- MY-DOCS:END --> will be stripped by algorithmic_compress because the negative lookahead fails to match the hyphenated ID. Concrete trigger: algorithmic_compress('<\!-- MY-DOCS:START -->\nContent\n<\!-- MY-DOCS:END -->') returns 'Content' with markers deleted. Fix: change \w+ to [\w-]+ in the lookahead pattern.

title: --validate CLI is a no-op: validates freshly-scanned tree against same disk
description: In cli.py:157-193, the --validate workflow does: (1) scan docs fresh from disk, (2) assign tiers, (3) validate that same tree against the same disk. Since the DocTree was just built from the files on disk, missing_files will always be empty (all files exist — we just found them) and stale_entries will always be empty (hashes match — we just computed them). The only check that partially works is extra_files, but even that has issues (see #118). Concrete trigger: delete a doc file, then run 'agent-index --validate --config agent-index.yaml' — it will NOT detect the deletion because it rescans first. The feature should load a previously saved index instead of scanning fresh.

title: Add whitespace and visual density axis
description: No axis tests VISUAL DENSITY of the documentation index. Need: (1) compact vs spacious formatting (single newline vs double newline between entries), (2) indentation depth (2-space vs 4-space vs tabs), (3) separator styles (horizontal rules, blank lines, section markers like '---'), (4) list style (bullet lists vs numbered lists vs no lists), (5) information density per line (one fact per line vs dense paragraphs). This is the lowest-hanging fruit for doc authors — it requires zero content changes, only whitespace/formatting tweaks. LLM tokenizers handle whitespace differently across models, making this potentially model-specific.

title: inject_into_file non-idempotent when appending to file without markers
description: In output.py:338-343, when inject_into_file is called on an existing file that has no markers, content is appended raw without wrapping in START/END markers. The new-file path (line 326) correctly wraps with markers (fixed in commit 42f2c26), but this append path was missed. Concrete trigger: call inject_into_file(path, 'v1') on an existing file without markers, then call inject_into_file(path, 'v2') again — the file now contains both 'v1' and 'v2' appended, with no way to replace. Each subsequent call adds another copy. Fix: wrap appended content with markers, matching the new-file behavior.

title: --validate CLI ignores config file_extensions and ignore_patterns
description: In cli.py:193, the --validate path calls validate_index(doc_tree, scan_path) without passing file_extensions or ignore_patterns from the config. Even though validate_index accepts these params (added in commit 245ef36), the CLI doesn't forward them. Concrete trigger: config has ignore_patterns: ['vendor', 'dist'] but validate uses defaults (['node_modules', '__pycache__', '.git', '.venv']). Files in vendor/ or dist/ appear as false-positive extra_files. Fix: pass config.file_extensions and config.ignore_patterns to validate_index.

title: validate and autodetect rglob lacks symlink loop protection
description: In validate.py:122 (_collect_disk_files) and autodetect.py:194 (_collect_doc_files), both use root.rglob('*') which follows symlinks by default. Unlike scanner.py which has explicit loop detection via visited_dirs set (lines 120-129), these modules have no protection. Concrete trigger: create a symlink loop (e.g., 'ln -s ../docs docs/self') and run auto-detect or validate — rglob will recurse infinitely until hitting OS limits or crashing. Fix: either use rglob with follow_symlinks=False (Python 3.13+) or implement visited-path tracking like the scanner does.

title: Phase C: Premium custom scrollbar
transform_tree incremental skip returns untransformed content on fresh scans
description: In transform.py:296-302, when transform_tree skips a file because its content_hash matches state, it uses the DocFile from the CURRENT doc_tree (new_files[rel_path] = doc). If the current tree came from a fresh scan (not a previously transformed tree), this is the original untransformed content. The state only stores hashes, not transformed content. Concrete trigger: (1) scan + transform tree + save state, (2) scan again (fresh), (3) transform with saved state — skipped files have raw content, not their previously transformed versions. Fix: state needs to store either transformed content or transformed hashes, or the caller must persist and pass the transformed tree.

title: _resolve_strategy silently falls back to passthrough for unrecognized LLM strategy
description: In transform.py:201-207, _resolve_strategy falls through to passthrough when step.type=='llm' but step.strategy is not in _STRATEGY_MAP. The default strategy value on TransformStep is 'default', which has no entry in the map. Concrete trigger: TransformStep(type='llm') or config with transform_steps: [{type: llm}] — silently applies passthrough with no warning or error. User thinks LLM compression is running but gets raw content. Fix: raise ValueError or log a warning when strategy is not found, or add 'default' to _STRATEGY_MAP mapping to a sensible default.

title: Refinement phase (Phase 3) does not compute or report interaction effects
description: Phase 3 (run_refinement in pipeline.py lines 245-281) runs full factorial on top-K factors but only stores raw trial results. It does not: (1) compute 2-way interaction effects between factors, (2) identify which factor combinations are synergistic or antagonistic, (3) report whether the additive model assumption holds, (4) produce any analysis beyond what comes from the orchestrator. The interaction_analysis.py module has Lenth method and half-normal plot code but it's not integrated into Phase 3. The md_renderer.py Taguchi sections (10-14) only render screening phase analysis. Need: Phase 3 should compute interaction effects from the full factorial data and render them in the report.

title: autodetect _classify_file directory names override filename classification
description: In autodetect.py:221-233, _classify_file iterates over ALL path components (directories + filename) left-to-right. The first keyword match wins. Directory names can override more relevant filename-based classification. Concrete trigger: _classify_file('api/getting-started.md') returns 'reference' because 'api' directory matches _REFERENCE_KEYWORDS before the filename 'getting-started' (which would match _REQUIRED_KEYWORDS). Similarly, 'reference/quickstart.md' returns 'reference' not 'required'. Fix: check filename first, or check required keywords across all components before checking reference keywords.

title: --validate CLI renders unused index_content (dead code)
description: In cli.py:186-192, the --validate path computes index_content = render_index(...) but never uses the variable. This is dead code that wastes computation (sorting files, rendering markdown). The variable was likely left over from an earlier design where validate compared rendered output. Fix: remove the sort_files_bluf and render_index calls, or if validation should compare rendered output, actually use index_content.

title: Add comparative benchmark against existing doc optimization methods
description: The framework has no external validation — no comparison to existing documentation quality standards or tools. Need: (1) benchmark against Google's developer documentation style guide recommendations, (2) compare against Divio's documentation system (tutorials/how-to/reference/explanation), (3) test whether Diataxis-style formatting scores differently from ad-hoc formatting, (4) correlate Taguchi-optimal formats with human-rated documentation quality (e.g., ReadTheDocs ratings), (5) A/B test: run the same tasks with human-written 'best practice' docs vs Taguchi-optimized docs. This positions the framework as either validating or challenging industry best practices — either outcome is a publishable result.

title: Add incremental update evaluation (doc change impact analysis)
description: Documentation changes constantly. The framework can't answer: 'If I update one page, how does it affect overall agent performance?' Need: (1) delta-evaluation mode — add/modify/delete one doc and re-score without full re-run, (2) change impact prediction — estimate score impact from doc diffs, (3) regression detection — alert when a doc update degrades performance on specific task types, (4) 'documentation coverage' metric — which areas of the doc corpus contribute most to which task types. This enables CI/CD integration: run agent-evals on doc PRs to catch regressions before merge. Currently the framework only supports full-corpus evaluation.

title: No experiment export/import format for reproducibility sharing
description: While individual runs are stored in the local SQLite observatory DB with full config and trial data, there is no way to export a complete experiment specification as a portable artifact that someone else could reproduce. Need: an 'agent-evals export <run_id>' command that produces a self-contained JSON/YAML bundle including: (1) full EvalRunConfig, (2) model versions used, (3) variant specifications, (4) task IDs and definitions, (5) all trial results, (6) Taguchi analysis if applicable. And a corresponding 'agent-evals import <bundle>' to load into another observatory instance for comparison.

title: Add retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chunking strategy evaluation
description: Most production systems don't inject full docs — they use RAG with embedding-based retrieval. The framework doesn't test how doc FORMAT interacts with CHUNKING STRATEGY. Need: (1) chunking strategies as a new axis (fixed-size, semantic, heading-based, sliding window), (2) test which doc formats chunk well (markdown tables may split badly), (3) measure retrieval recall per variant when using embedding search, (4) test format × chunk-size interactions (e.g., YAML metadata helps with small chunks by preserving context), (5) compare full-injection vs top-K-chunks vs hierarchical retrieval. This bridges the gap between the current 'stuff everything in the prompt' approach and how docs are actually consumed in production RAG pipelines.
close_reason: Superseded by Context Strategy Phase 3 (RAG Mode)

title: CostTracker budget pause not wired to EvalRunner signal handling
description: CostTracker.check_budget() returns True when projected cost exceeds 2x budget, and should_pause() is an alias. However, tracing the runner.py code, the CostTracker is only used in the orchestrator/tracker layer for observatory events (burn_rate_alert, model_budget_exceeded) — it's not wired to actually pause or stop the EvalRunner's ThreadPoolExecutor. The runner has graceful shutdown via SIGINT/SIGTERM but no budget-triggered pause. The budget flag is accepted by the CLI (--budget) but the runner will continue executing trials past the budget limit. Need: wire CostTracker.should_pause() into the runner's trial loop to stop accepting new work when budget is exceeded.

title: Phase C: Provider combobox
Dry-run cost estimation not available for pipeline mode
description: The --dry-run flag in cli.py (lines 612-670) only handles 'full' mode (logs config) and 'taguchi' mode (shows OA design). It does not estimate total cost for pipeline mode (3-phase: screening + confirmation + refinement). Users planning a full DOE pipeline cannot estimate costs before committing. A pipeline dry-run should estimate: Phase 1 cost (OA rows × tasks × screening_reps), Phase 2 cost (1 × tasks × confirmation_reps), Phase 3 cost (top_k^levels × tasks × refinement_reps), and the grand total across all three phases.

title: RobustnessTask missing fuzzy matching despite claiming FactExtraction parity
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/robustness.py

The module docstring says 'Reuses the same scoring logic as FactExtractionTask' but the implementation is missing two fuzzy matching layers present in fact_extraction.py:
- Layer 3: token_set_ratio >= 85 → 0.9
- Layer 4: token_set_ratio >= 70 → 0.7

RobustnessTask only has: exact match → 1.0, alias match → 1.0, keyword fallback → fraction.
FactExtractionTask has: exact → 1.0, alias → 1.0, fuzzy(>=85) → 0.9, fuzzy(>=70) → 0.7, keyword → fraction.

This is ironic: robustness tasks test PERTURBED inputs (typos, paraphrases) where fuzzy matching is most needed, but they have LESS scoring flexibility than the non-perturbed fact_extraction tasks.

Example: expected_answer='CacheConfig default_ttl is 300 seconds', LLM response='The CacheConfig defaults to a TTL of 300 seconds'. In fact_extraction, token_set_ratio would give >=85 → score 0.9. In robustness, exact match fails, aliases fail, keyword fallback gives ~0.6.

Impact: Robustness scores are systematically depressed vs equivalent fact_extraction tasks. This biases Taguchi analysis by making robustness tasks appear artificially harder.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: CodeGenerationTask syntax bonus is Python-only, penalizes non-Python tasks
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/code_generation.py

_check_syntax() uses ast.parse() which only validates Python syntax. Non-Python code generation tasks always get syntax_bonus=0.0, permanently losing 10% of their maximum score (0.1 out of 1.0 in the formula: match_rate*0.7 + (1-violation_rate)*0.2 + syntax_bonus*0.1).

Affected gold standard task: code_generation_018 asks for a YAML pipeline definition. Even a perfect YAML response scores at most 0.9 because ast.parse(yaml_content) raises SyntaxError.

Fix options:
1. Detect language from the code block fence tag (python/yaml/sql/etc) and only validate Python
2. Skip syntax bonus for tasks without a Python-centric entry_point
3. Use a multi-language syntax checker
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: XrefDense 'Referenced by:' label is semantically reversed
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/variants/xref_dense.py (lines 102-109)

The 'Referenced by:' section is computed by checking which file stems appear in the CURRENT file's content. This finds files that the current file REFERENCES (outgoing links), NOT files that reference the current file (incoming links).

The label should be 'References:' not 'Referenced by:'.

Example: If errors.md mentions 'auth' and 'config' in its content, it renders as:
  errors.md Referenced by: auth.md, config.md
This implies auth.md and config.md reference errors.md, but actually errors.md references them.

The 'See also:' section already partially covers incoming references (files that mention this file's stem), creating further semantic confusion between the two labels.

Impact: Misleading cross-reference labels could confuse the LLM during agentic/retrieval tasks. The LLM might follow 'Referenced by' links expecting incoming references but finding outgoing ones.

title: Negative scorer gives full marks to responses that abstain AND hallucinate
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/tasks/negative.py

The scorer uses simple substring matching: any(p in response_lower for p in _FIRM_REFUSAL). It checks for presence of refusal phrases but does NOT check whether the response ALSO provides a confident answer.

A response like 'The timeout is not mentioned explicitly in the documentation, but based on Redis defaults it is likely 60 seconds' contains 'not mentioned' and scores 1.0 (firm refusal), despite providing a hallucinated answer. This is a partial-abstention-then-hallucination pattern that should score lower (e.g., 0.3-0.5) rather than getting full credit.

Phrases most susceptible to false positives in non-refusal contexts:
- 'not mentioned' / 'not specified' / 'not available' — can appear in hedging before answering
- 'not found' — can appear as 'the information was not found to directly state...'
- 'not documented' — 'while not documented explicitly, it appears to be...'

The current scorer rewards any response that includes a refusal phrase, even if the response then proceeds to hallucinate an answer. A more robust scorer would check whether the response primarily abstains vs primarily answers.
close_reason: NOT A BUG: NegativeTask scoring uses a tiered priority system with early returns (negative.py:143-166). Firm refusal phrases return 1.0 immediately by design — the abstention intent is prioritized. This is a deliberate design choice, not a bug.

title: CompositeVariant concatenates full independent renders, inflating prompt 10x
description:
File: agent-evals/src/agent_evals/variants/composite.py

CompositeVariant.render() calls each component's render(doc_tree) independently, then concatenates with '\n\n'. Since every axis (1-10) produces a COMPLETE rendering of the doc_tree, a 10-axis Taguchi composite produces 10 separate renderings of the same documentation (e.g., a flat list + YAML output + pipe-delimited table + noise-augmented list + section-level entries + ...).

This means:
1. The prompt is ~10x longer than any single variant, consuming excessive tokens
2. The LLM sees the same documentation repeated 10 different ways — unlike any real documentation format
3. Taguchi S/N ratios measure the combined effect of 10 concatenated renderings, not isolated axis effects
4. The additivity assumption (axes are independent) is violated since each axis's contribution depends on how much context the other 9 renderings consume

Expected behavior: A composite should produce ONE rendering that combines properties from each axis (e.g., YAML format + section granularity + noise injection + BLUF ordering), not 10 independent renderings concatenated together.

Fix: Refactor CompositeVariant to use a pipeline/decorator pattern where axes modify a single base rendering rather than each producing an independent one. For example: scale selects files → structure organizes them → format renders → noise adds distractors → position reorders → metadata enriches.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: LLM judge uses evaluation model instead of JUDGE_MODEL
description:
Two issues in runner.py:799-806 (_call_judge method):

1. Judge model not passed to LLM call: Code retrieves self._config.judge_model but calls self._client.complete(messages) WITHOUT passing model= kwarg. The complete() method uses self.model (the evaluation model) when no model= kwarg is provided. Fix: change line 806 to self._client.complete(messages, model=judge_model).content

2. No --judge-model CLI flag: There is no CLI flag to configure the judge model. Only --judge-mode and --judge-sample-rate exist. The judge model should be selectable via --judge-model CLI flag (defaulting to openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini) and configurable in YAML.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: Pipeline confirmation phase loses prediction interval from screening
description: In pipeline.py run_confirmation() (lines 219-222), the OptimalPrediction is reconstructed with only optimal_assignment and predicted_sn. The prediction_interval and se_prediction computed during screening are NOT carried forward. validate_confirmation() then falls back to hardcoded +/-1.0 dB interval and se=1.0, making confirmation validation meaningless. Fix: store prediction_interval and se_prediction in PhaseResult during screening and pass them to the reconstructed OptimalPrediction.
close_reason: FIXED: Prediction interval IS preserved. Confirmation phase correctly receives screening_result.optimal and screening_result.predicted_sn (pipeline.py:240-243), passes to validate_confirmation() which uses the interval (analysis.py:534-538).

title: Bug: Retrieval fuzzy match inflates scores - same path matches multiple expected
description: In retrieval.py lines 110-115, the fuzzy basename matching loop breaks after matching an extracted path to one expected path, but does NOT remove the extracted path from unmatched_extracted. The same extracted file can match multiple expected files. Example: expected=[src/auth.py, lib/auth.py], extracted=[vendor/auth.py] gives fuzzy_hits=1.0 when only 0.5 is deserved. This can make precision and recall exceed 1.0 before clamping. Fix: remove matched extracted paths from unmatched_extracted after each basename match.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: RobustnessTask missing fuzzy matching despite docstring claim
description: robustness.py docstring says 'Reuses the same scoring logic as FactExtractionTask' but only implements exact/alias/keyword fallback. FactExtractionTask has a 4-layer cascade: exact -> alias -> fuzzy@85 (0.9) -> fuzzy@70 (0.7) -> keyword. RobustnessTask skips the rapidfuzz layers entirely. This is especially problematic because robustness tasks test perturbed inputs (typos, paraphrases) where fuzzy matching matters most. A response scoring 0.9 in FactExtraction could score much lower in Robustness due to the missing fuzzy layer.

title: Phase C: Premium loading skeleton
Bug: Pipeline refinement phase never analyzes its trial results
description: In pipeline.py run_refinement() (lines 274-281), the PhaseResult is returned with only raw trials - no main_effects, anova, optimal, or significant_factors are computed. The final_optimal on line 392 always falls back to screening.optimal because refinement.optimal is always None. This means the refinement phase (full factorial on top-K factors) runs expensive trials but never identifies whether a different combination is better than the screening prediction. Fix: add analysis computation to run_refinement() similar to run_screening().
close_reason: Fixed and verified: all 3460 tests pass

title: Bug: Silent rate-limit retry uses deterministic backoff (thundering herd)
description: PARTIALLY FIXED: The retryable exception path (client.py:186-192) correctly uses random.uniform(0, max_delay) for jitter. However, the silent rate-limit retry path (client.py:151-159) for content=None responses still uses deterministic exponential backoff: delay = RETRY_BASE_DELAY * (2 ** attempt) with no jitter. When multiple threads hit rate limits simultaneously, they all retry at the exact same time. Fix: change line 153 to use random.uniform(0, delay) like the exception path.
close_reason: Fixed: silent rate-limit retry now uses random.uniform(0, max_delay) jitter

title: Bug: TaguchiRunner silently swallows all exceptions as failed trials
description: In taguchi/runner.py line 337, _run_trial() catches all Exception types and returns an error TrialResult with score=0.0. Programming bugs (TypeError, AttributeError, KeyError) are silently recorded as 'failed trials' instead of propagating. Compare with EvalRunner._run_trial() which lets exceptions propagate to the caller. This makes debugging very difficult - a bug in task.build_prompt() or task.score_response() appears as a low score rather than a crash. Fix: only catch expected exceptions (LLM errors, network errors) or re-raise non-retriable errors.

title: Bug: Report aggregator uses z=1.96 for confidence intervals regardless of sample size
description: In reports/aggregator.py lines 65-68, confidence intervals use z=1.96 (normal approximation) even for small samples (2-30 trials). For n=2, the correct t-distribution multiplier is ~12.7, not 1.96. This makes confidence intervals far too narrow for small samples, potentially leading to false conclusions about variant differences. Fix: use scipy.stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=count-1) instead of the hardcoded 1.96 multiplier.

title: Bug: Retrieval file path regex only matches 8 extensions
description: In retrieval.py lines 19-22, _FILE_PATH_PATTERN only matches: md|py|yaml|yml|json|toml|txt|rst|html. Missing common extensions: .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .css, .scss, .go, .rs, .java, .xml, .cfg, .ini, .sh, .bash, .dockerfile, .env, .rb, .php, .c, .cpp, .h. Any retrieval task with expected files using these extensions will fail to extract them from responses, yielding score=0.0. Fix: expand the extension list or use a more permissive pattern like [\w.-]+\.\w{1,10}.

title: Bug: CompositeVariant.teardown() skips remaining components on exception
description: In variants/composite.py lines 87-90, teardown() iterates components without try/except per component. If any component's teardown() raises, remaining components are never torn down. Same issue exists in setup() (lines 82-85) - no rollback of already-setup components on partial failure. Compare with EvalRunner.run() (runner.py:385-393) and TaguchiRunner (taguchi/runner.py:240-247) which wrap individual teardowns. Fix: wrap each component teardown in try/except; add setup rollback logic.

title: [CS-P0] Fix level mapping bug in factors.py (mod N breaks OA balance)
description: HARD BLOCKER for Context Strategy plan. factors.py:120-123 uses raw_level % factor.n_levels to map OA column values to factor levels. Breaks balance when column_levels != factor.n_levels. 6 of 10 axes affected (2,4,7,8,9,10). Fix: dummy-level exclusion (standard Taguchi approach) — pad each factor to match OA column level count, exclude dummy-level rows from S/N and ANOVA. title: [CS-P1] Fix prediction interval bug in analysis.py (total variance instead of ANOVA MSE)

Current implementation: residual_var = sum((y - sn_mean)^2) / (n-1), should use ms_error from ANOVA with proper degrees of freedom. Produces methodologically incorrect prediction intervals (wrong df, includes factor-effect variance). See planning/CONTEXT_STRATEGY_PLAN.md Prerequisites P1.

If rankings differ, the framework needs dataset-conditional recommendations.

title: Replace regex tool scoring with actual tool execution in agentic tasks

Need: provide real tool definitions to the LLM (OpenAI tool_use / Claude tool_use), execute tool calls against the doc corpus, score based on actual retrieval quality and execution results, support multi-step tool chains. title: Add prompt caching evaluation to framework
description: Some doc formats cache better than others with Anthropic's prompt caching (90% cost savings on cache hits). The framework doesn't measure or optimize for cacheability. Need: track cache hit rates per variant, measure cost with/without caching, potentially add a caching-friendliness axis. Stable system message prefixes cache better — format choices that keep the doc index stable across tasks would score higher.

title: Add context competition testing (docs vs code vs history)
description: Real agents have code, conversation history, tool results, AND docs competing for context space. The framework tests docs in isolation — the system message is basically just the rendered index. Need: simulate realistic context budgets where docs must share space with code snippets, prior conversation turns, and tool output. Measure how format choices degrade when docs get only 30% of available context vs 100%.

title: Models page premium polish
Make variant rendering task-aware

Real doc systems surface different content depending on the query. Need: pass task context to render(), allow variants to adapt output based on task type/question, measure whether task-aware rendering outperforms static rendering. Affects IndexVariant.render() signature and CompositeVariant.

title: Measure axis interaction effects in Taguchi analysis
description: The Taguchi L50 design assumes axes are independent (additivity assumption). But interactions likely exist — e.g., granularity × scale (file-level is fine at 5 files but terrible at 200), format × metadata (YAML format may benefit more from rich metadata than markdown-list). Need: run follow-up experiments with interaction columns in the OA, or use full factorial on top-K factors (the refinement phase partially addresses this). Add interaction effect detection to the analysis module.

title: Add train/test split for generalization testing
description: All 355 gold tasks are used for both tuning and evaluation — no held-out test set. Results may not generalize to unseen tasks. Need: split gold tasks into train (for Taguchi screening) and test (for validation), or use cross-validation. Also need cross-corpus validation: train on synthetic fixture, test on real datasets. Currently all tasks in gold_standard/ are used together.

title: Validate task difficulty labels empirically
description: Tasks are labeled easy/medium/hard/edge but labels are never validated. Need: compute empirical difficulty from baseline variant scores, build difficulty curves per variant, detect variants that fail on easy tasks (regression) vs variants that handle hard tasks well (ceiling effects). Use the oracle and no-docs baselines to calibrate. Currently difficulty is just a metadata label with no scoring impact.

title: Add structured output scoring (JSON, code AST, schemas)
description: All scoring is text-based (keyword matching, regex, fuzzy string comparison). No JSON schema validation, no deep AST-level code comparison beyond basic syntax checks. Need: JSON mode / structured output support in LLMClient, schema-based scoring for code_generation and fact_extraction tasks, Pydantic model validation scoring. Would enable testing whether certain doc formats produce more parseable/structured agent responses.

title: Fix robustness tasks missing base_task_id metadata

The field exists in metadata but contains no useful data, breaking traceability — cannot link robustness tasks back to their base fact_extraction/retrieval tasks to measure perturbation impact. Need to populate base_task_id with the actual source task ID for each robustness task.

title: Fix variant teardown not called when continue_on_error=False

The teardown call should be in a finally block. Affects runner.py trial execution loop. Known issue documented in MEMORY.md.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Fix CompositeVariant header duplication on concatenation
description: CompositeVariant concatenates axis outputs with newline separator. When two format variants both output markdown headers (e.g., '# Documentation Index'), the result has duplicate headers that break markdown table parsing. Affected variants: format_markdown_table.py, format_yaml.py, format_markdown_list.py. Fix: either strip headers before concatenation or deduplicate them in CompositeVariant.render().

title: Apply Bonferroni/BH correction to Taguchi factor p-values
description: Taguchi ANOVA computes raw p-values for each factor but does NOT apply multiple comparisons correction. With 10 factors at alpha=0.05, expected false positive rate is ~40%. benjamini_hochberg() exists in statistics.py but is never called from analysis.py. Factor significance claims are statistically invalid without correction. Quick fix: apply BH correction to p-values before reporting significance in compute_main_effects/run_anova.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Handle bimodal/binary LLM scores in S/N ratio computation
description: LLM evaluation scores are bounded [0,1] and often bimodal (many 0s and 1s). The S/N ratio formula for larger_is_better uses mean(1/y^2) which goes to infinity for y=0. Current epsilon guard (1e-10) masks the degeneracy. ANOVA F-test assumes normality which is violated by bimodal data. Need: data transformation (arcsine/logit), non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis fallback, or document actual score distributions before claiming statistical significance.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Phase A: Table full width

LLM scores likely have interactions (e.g., format x metadata, granularity x scale). Prediction errors of 5-20% are plausible if interactions are large. Need: interaction test on top factors, or at minimum document the assumption and warn in reports. Prediction interval SE is also under-conservative.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

The docstring claims it's 'used to extract referenced paths' but the code only uses doc_tree.files.keys(). This is dead code that confuses the API. close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Fix local scanner size_bytes inconsistency with GitHub scanner
description: In scanner.py _create_docfile(), size_bytes is set from stat.st_size (raw disk bytes), while the GitHub scanner computes len(content.encode('utf-8')). On Windows, text mode reading converts CRLF to LF, so stat.st_size > len(content.encode('utf-8')). This inconsistency means size_bytes has different semantics depending on the source. Fix: use len(content.encode('utf-8')) in the local scanner too, matching the GitHub scanner and the actual content that content_hash is computed from.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Fix overly broad exception catch in autodetect _detect_project_name
description: In autodetect.py line 167, except (OSError, Exception) is equivalent to except Exception, swallowing all errors including unexpected ones like AttributeError or TypeError. This hides real bugs during project name detection from pyproject.toml. Fix: catch specific exceptions (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, KeyError).
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Fix pipeline confirmation phase hardcoded predicted_sn=0.0
description: In pipeline.py lines 206-209, run_confirmation() creates OptimalPrediction with predicted_sn=0.0 hardcoded instead of using the actual predicted_sn from the screening phase. This makes confirmation validation meaningless - sigma_deviation will be wrong, and within_interval uses a fallback interval instead of checking against the real prediction.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Fix thread-unsafe variant setup for Oracle/LMR baselines in EvalRunner
description: In runner.py _setup_variant_for_task() (lines 567-590), OracleBaseline and LengthMatchedRandomBaseline instances have their state mutated via set_relevant_docs()/set_target_tokens() from concurrent threads in ThreadPoolExecutor. These baseline variants store task-specific state as instance attributes (_relevant_docs, _target_tokens in baselines.py), so concurrent trials can overwrite each other's state, leading to incorrect scoring results.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Fix DiagnosticTracker snapshot averages diluted by resume offset
description: In diagnostics.py, when resuming a run, _completed starts at completed_offset but _total_api_ms/_total_trial_ms only accumulate from new trials. The snapshot() method computes avg_api_ms = total_new_api_ms / (offset + new_count), which dilutes the averages since the denominator includes previously-completed trials but the numerator only has timing data from new trials.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Phase B: Dual-handle range slider
Fix beam_search within_parity flags not updated after Holm-Bonferroni
description: In beam_search.py select_beam() (lines 148-189), candidate.within_parity flags are set based on raw p-values BEFORE the Holm-Bonferroni correction is applied at lines 188-189. After correction, the pairwise_tests list gets updated p-values but the candidate flags still reflect the uncorrected values. This can cause candidates to be incorrectly marked as within parity when their corrected p-values would reject the null hypothesis.
close_reason: Fix committed and reviewed by team

title: Implement phase result persistence in observatory store
Add cross-model consistency testing as a first-class evaluation dimension
description: The framework supports multi-model via the Taguchi model factor, but doesn't measure CROSS-MODEL CONSISTENCY — whether the same doc format produces reliably good results across different model families (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama) or only excels on one. Need: (1) consistency metrics per variant across models (Kendall's W concordance, ICC), (2) model-family interaction analysis — does format X work great on Claude but terribly on GPT-4?, (3) robustness-to-model-change scores so doc authors can pick formats that are 'model-portable', (4) architecture-aware analysis (transformer size, context window implementation). This would be the killer feature for DevRel teams who can't control which model their users deploy against their docs.

title: Add context window pressure testing (degradation curves)
description: No axis tests how format choices degrade as context fills up. A format might score great at 4K tokens but collapse at 128K when buried in noise. Need: (1) generate degradation curves per variant — score at 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90% context utilization, (2) measure the 'lost in the middle' effect per format, (3) identify formats that degrade gracefully vs cliff-edge failures, (4) test primacy/recency bias per format — does putting docs at the start vs end of a large context change results?, (5) simulate realistic context budgets (8K, 32K, 128K, 200K). This is critical because real-world agents often operate near context limits. The scale axis (6) only varies doc COUNT, not context PRESSURE relative to the model's window.
close_reason: Superseded by Context Strategy Phase 2 (System Prompt Mode)

title: Add latency/cost-normalized scoring dimension
description: The framework records latency_seconds and cost per trial but doesn't incorporate them into optimization. A variant scoring 0.95 accuracy at 200K tokens and $0.50/query is worse than one scoring 0.90 at 20K tokens and $0.05/query. Need: (1) Pareto-frontier analysis: accuracy vs cost vs latency, (2) cost-efficiency composite scores (accuracy per dollar), (3) token-efficiency metrics (accuracy per 1K tokens), (4) Taguchi quality loss function that penalizes high-cost variants, (5) budget-constrained optimization: 'best format if I can only spend $X per query'. Currently the scoring module uses composite_score() that only weighs task types, completely ignoring economic factors. For production deployments this is the most important dimension after raw accuracy.

title: Add LLM-as-judge scoring to replace heuristic keyword matching
description: Every task type uses heuristic scoring: keyword matching, regex, fuzzy string comparison. This systematically undervalues correct answers phrased differently and overvalues keyword-stuffed wrong answers. The framework has a 2% judge sampling rate (JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE=50) but doesn't use judge scores for optimization. Need: (1) LLM-as-judge as the PRIMARY scoring method (not 2% sample), (2) calibrate heuristic vs judge agreement rates per task type, (3) use judge scores in Taguchi S/N computation, (4) multi-judge consensus for high-stakes comparisons, (5) judge prompt templates per task type (fact extraction needs different rubric than code generation). The heuristic scoring systematically biases the framework — a variant that produces well-written natural language answers may score LOWER than one that produces keyword-rich but unhelpful responses. This undermines all results.
